# What this document does

One SEIR BiLSTM that combines the two earlier lines of work:

| | v3 | v5 | **v6 (this model)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Days it reads | 30 to 365, beginning, middle or end | 61, from the beginning | **30 to 365, beginning, middle or end** |
| Training curves | every new case | reported cases, new noise every time | **reported cases, new noise every time** |
| Ranges | share exposed 1-40%, incubation 3-21 days, R0 1-5 | share exposed 0.1-40%, incubation 1-21, R0 0.8-5 | **same as v5** |
| Also estimates | shares exposed, infectious, recovered at the window start | reported share, noise, weekday swing | **all of these** |
| R0 range | no | yes | **yes** |

How it is trained:

1. **Simulate** `r format(params$n_sims, big.mark = ",")` SEIR epidemics of `r params$n_days` days
   (true daily cases, and the shares exposed, infectious and recovered on every day). Each
   epidemic also gets a reported share, a noise level and a weekday swing.
2. **Every training step** picks a window: a length between `r params$window_min` and
   `r params$window_max` days (drawn uniformly) and a start anywhere inside the epidemic's
   informative days (before its first week without cases). Then it makes **new reported
   cases** for that window: it keeps the reported share of the cases, adds a weekly
   pattern and random noise. So the network never sees the same window or the same noise
   twice.
3. The network learns R0 (and ptran), the reported share, the noise level, the weekday
   swing and the state at the window start. The shares exposed, infectious and recovered
   are learned on the log scale, so small epidemics (like flu admissions) are readable.

Known values, as before: `n`, `recov`, `incub`.

# Step 1: simulate

```{r simulate}
# Days before the first run of k days without cases (the whole curve if none).
informative_days <- function(curve, k = STOP_ZEROS) {
  r   <- rle(as.numeric(curve) == 0)
  hit <- which(r$values & r$lengths >= k)[1]
  if (is.na(hit)) length(curve) else sum(r$lengths[seq_len(hit)]) - r$lengths[hit]
}

# True daily cases and the shares exposed, infectious and recovered at the start
# of each day; the reporting parameters are drawn too (applied later).
simulate_states <- function(n_sims, seed) {
  base <- seir_simulator(ndays = N_DAYS, priors = PRIORS)
  sim  <- new_simulator(base$sample_parameters, function(parameters, seed) {
    m <- epiworldR::ModelSEIRCONN(
      name = "sim", n = parameters$n, prevalence = parameters$preval,
      contact_rate = parameters$crate, incubation_days = parameters$incub,
      transmission_rate = parameters$ptran, recovery_rate = parameters$recov
    )
    epiworldR::verbose_off(m)
    epiworldR::run(m, ndays = N_DAYS + 1L, seed = seed)
    h <- epiworldR::get_hist_total(m)
    h <- h[order(h$date), ]
    at_start <- function(state) h$counts[h$state == state][seq_len(N_DAYS)] / parameters$n
    c(get_incidence(m, N_DAYS), at_start("Exposed"), at_start("Infected"), at_start("Recovered"))
  }, type = "SEIR")
  simulate_training_data(sim, n_sims = n_sims, seed = seed)
}

# A bank of n_keep epidemics, simulated in chunks on SIM_CORES cores (chunk k
# uses seed + k - 1). reported = TRUE turns the true cases into reported cases.
# Epidemics with fewer than MIN_CASES (expected) reported cases are dropped.
simulate_bank <- function(n_keep, seed, reported) {
  n_draw <- ceiling(1.15 * n_keep)
  sizes  <- diff(round(seq(0, n_draw, length.out = max(SIM_CORES, 1) + 1)))
  chunks <- parallel::mclapply(seq_along(sizes), function(k) simulate_states(sizes[k], seed + k - 1),
                               mc.cores = max(SIM_CORES, 1))
  failed <- vapply(chunks, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
  if (any(failed)) stop("Simulation chunk(s) failed: ", paste(which(failed), collapse = ", "))
  theta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, `[[`, "theta"))
  part  <- function(j) do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, function(x) x$observations[, j * N_DAYS + seq_len(N_DAYS), drop = FALSE]))
  cases <- part(0)
  states <- setNames(lapply(1:3, part), STATES)
  rm(chunks)
  if (reported) {
    set.seed(seed)
    cases <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(cases)), function(i)
      observe_cases(cases[i, ], theta$report_rate[i], theta$overdispersion[i], theta$weekday_sd[i]),
      numeric(N_DAYS)))
    n_reported <- rowSums(cases)
  } else {
    n_reported <- theta$report_rate * rowSums(cases)
  }
  keep <- which(n_reported >= MIN_CASES)
  if (length(keep) < n_keep) stop("Only ", length(keep), " epidemics with enough cases.")
  keep <- keep[seq_len(n_keep)]
  theta <- theta[keep, ]
  rownames(theta) <- NULL
  for (v in c("preval", "report_rate", "overdispersion")) theta[[paste0("log_", v)]] <- log(theta[[v]])
  list(theta = theta, cases = cases[keep, , drop = FALSE],
       states = lapply(states, function(s) s[keep, , drop = FALSE]),
       dropped_share = mean(n_reported < MIN_CASES))
}

write_matrix <- function(x, file) data.table::fwrite(as.data.frame(round(x, 5)), file)
train_files <- c(theta = file.path(BANK_DIR, "seir_theta.csv"), cases = file.path(BANK_DIR, "seir_observations.csv"),
                 setNames(file.path(BANK_DIR, paste0("seir_", STATE_TARGETS, ".csv")), STATE_TARGETS))

fresh_bank <- FALSE
if (!all(file.exists(train_files)) || nrow(data.table::fread(train_files[["theta"]], select = 1L)) != N_SIMS) {
  t_sim <- system.time(b <- simulate_bank(N_SIMS, BANK_SEED, reported = FALSE))
  dir.create(BANK_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  data.table::fwrite(b$theta, train_files[["theta"]])
  write_matrix(b$cases, train_files[["cases"]])
  for (k in seq_along(STATES)) write_matrix(log(b$states[[k]] + STATE_OFFSET), train_files[[STATE_TARGETS[k]]])
  writeLines(as.character(c(round(t_sim[["elapsed"]]), b$dropped_share)), file.path(BANK_DIR, "simulation_seconds_and_dropped_share.txt"))
  rm(b); gc()
  fresh_bank <- TRUE
}

# Test and calibration epidemics: reported cases. The calibration bank keeps one
# random window per epidemic (length and start drawn as in training).
test_file  <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "test_bank.rds")
calib_file <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "calibration_windows.rds")
if (!file.exists(test_file)) {
  b <- simulate_bank(N_TEST, TEST_SEED, reported = TRUE)
  saveRDS(b, test_file)
}
if (!file.exists(calib_file)) {
  t_cal <- system.time(b <- simulate_bank(N_CALIB, CALIB_SEED, reported = TRUE))
  set.seed(CALIB_SEED)
  active <- apply(b$cases, 1, informative_days)
  use <- which(active >= WINDOW_MIN)
  L <- vapply(use, function(i) if (min(WINDOW_MAX, active[i]) == WINDOW_MIN) WINDOW_MIN else
    sample(WINDOW_MIN:min(WINDOW_MAX, active[i]), 1), numeric(1))
  s <- vapply(seq_along(use), function(j) sample.int(active[use[j]] - L[j] + 1, 1), numeric(1))
  saveRDS(list(
    theta = b$theta[use, ], start = s, length = L,
    cases = lapply(seq_along(use), function(j) b$cases[use[j], s[j]:(s[j] + L[j] - 1)]),
    state = data.frame(lapply(b$states, function(m) m[cbind(use, s)])),
    seconds = t_cal[["elapsed"]]
  ), calib_file)
  rm(b); gc()
}
test  <- readRDS(test_file)
calib <- readRDS(calib_file)
info  <- readLines(file.path(BANK_DIR, "simulation_seconds_and_dropped_share.txt"))
cat("Training bank:", format(N_SIMS, big.mark = ","), "epidemics, simulated in", round(as.numeric(info[1]) / 60, 1),
    "minutes;", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * as.numeric(info[2])), "dropped (fewer than", MIN_CASES, "reported cases)\n")
cat("Calibration windows:", format(length(calib$cases), big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

# Step 2: train

One model per seed; with `ensemble` the report uses the average of all seeds.

```{r train}
model_dirs <- file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("model_seed_", SEEDS))
model_matches <- function(dir, seed) {
  f <- file.path(dir, "model_config.json")
  if (!file.exists(file.path(dir, "model.pt")) || !file.exists(f)) return(FALSE)
  cfg <- jsonlite::read_json(f)
  cfg$epochs == EPOCHS && cfg$seed == seed && isTRUE(cfg$variable_length) && isTRUE(cfg$observation_noise) &&
    cfg$window_min == WINDOW_MIN && cfg$window_max == WINDOW_MAX && cfg$window_stop_zeros == STOP_ZEROS &&
    identical(unlist(cfg$target_names), c(TARGETS, STATE_TARGETS)) &&
    cfg$hidden_size == HIDDEN_SIZE && cfg$batch_size == BATCH_SIZE &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(cfg$learning_rate, LEARNING_RATE))
}
for (i in seq_along(SEEDS)) {
  if (RETRAIN || fresh_bank || !model_matches(model_dirs[i], SEEDS[i])) {
    t <- system.time(train_bilstm_calibrator(
      name = "seir", known_names = KNOWN, target_names = TARGETS, type = "SEIR",
      parameter_file = train_files[["theta"]], observation_file = train_files[["cases"]],
      output_dir = model_dirs[i], epochs = EPOCHS, batch_size = BATCH_SIZE, learning_rate = LEARNING_RATE,
      seed = SEEDS[i], hidden_size = HIDDEN_SIZE, num_layers = NUM_LAYERS, dropout = DROPOUT,
      physics_weight = 0, incidence_max = INCIDENCE_MAX, incidence_transform = INCIDENCE_TRANSFORM,
      output_activation = OUTPUT_ACTIVATION, window_min = WINDOW_MIN, window_max = WINDOW_MAX,
      window_stop_zeros = STOP_ZEROS, state_files = train_files[STATE_TARGETS], grad_clip = GRAD_CLIP,
      observation_noise = TRUE, device = params$device
    ))
    writeLines(as.character(round(t[["elapsed"]])), file.path(model_dirs[i], "training_seconds.txt"))
  }
}
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(SEEDS), function(i) {
  cfg <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(model_dirs[i], "model_config.json"))
  data.frame(seed = SEEDS[i], best_epoch = cfg$best_epoch, trained_on = cfg$device,
             minutes = round(as.numeric(readLines(file.path(model_dirs[i], "training_seconds.txt"))) / 60))
})), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Step 3: new simulated epidemics

```{r predict-helpers}
# Average of several models' estimates (curves of any lengths for v3 and v6);
# crate is computed from the averaged R0 and ptran. v6 learned log(share +
# STATE_OFFSET), so its state shares get the offset removed.
predict_models <- function(dirs, curves, known, state_offset = 0) {
  known <- as.data.frame(known)[, KNOWN, drop = FALSE]
  ests  <- lapply(dirs, function(d) bilstm_predict_many(d, curves, known, device = params$device))
  avg   <- Reduce(`+`, ests) / length(ests)
  avg$crate <- avg$R0 * known$recov / avg$ptran
  for (s in STATES) if (s %in% names(avg)) avg[[s]] <- pmax(avg[[s]] - state_offset, 0)
  avg
}
predict_v6 <- function(dirs, curves, known) predict_models(dirs, curves, known, state_offset = STATE_OFFSET)
V6_DIRS  <- if (ENSEMBLE) model_dirs else model_dirs[1]
V6_LABEL <- if (ENSEMBLE) sprintf("SEIR v6 (average of %d seeds)", length(SEEDS)) else "SEIR v6"

# The fast path gives the same numbers as calibrate().
cal <- bilstm_calibrator(model_dirs[1], known_names = KNOWN, type = "SEIR", device = params$device)
y1  <- test$cases[1, 1:90]
one <- calibrate(y1, cal, n = test$theta$n[1], recov = test$theta$recov[1], incub = test$theta$incub[1])
many <- predict_v6(model_dirs[1], list(y1), test$theta[1, ])
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(one[c("R0", "report_rate")]), unname(unlist(many[1, c("R0", "report_rate")])),
                           tolerance = 1e-5)))
```

Windows of each length, at the beginning, middle and end of each test epidemic's
informative days (before its first week without reported cases). v3 was trained on every
case, not on reported cases; v5 only reads 61 days from the beginning.

```{r grid}
active <- apply(test$cases, 1, informative_days)
win_start <- function(pos, L, a) switch(pos, beginning = 1, middle = floor((a - L) / 2) + 1, end = a - L + 1)
grid <- expand.grid(length = GRID_LENGTHS, position = POSITIONS, curve = seq_len(N_TEST), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
grid <- grid[active[grid$curve] >= grid$length, ]
grid$start <- mapply(win_start, grid$position, grid$length, active[grid$curve])
windows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(k) test$cases[grid$curve[k], grid$start[k]:(grid$start[k] + grid$length[k] - 1)])
known_g <- test$theta[grid$curve, KNOWN]

e6 <- predict_v6(V6_DIRS, windows, known_g)
e3 <- predict_models(V3_DIRS, windows, known_g)
b61 <- which(grid$length == 61 & grid$position == "beginning")
e5 <- predict_models(V5_DIRS, do.call(rbind, windows[b61]), known_g[b61, ])

truth_R0 <- test$theta$R0[grid$curve]
grid_est <- rbind(
  data.frame(model = V6_LABEL, grid, R0 = e6$R0),
  data.frame(model = "v3 (any length, every case)", grid, R0 = e3$R0),
  data.frame(model = "v5 (61 days, reported cases)", grid[b61, ], R0 = e5$R0)
)
grid_est$R0_abs_error <- abs(grid_est$R0 - test$theta$R0[grid_est$curve])
r0_tab <- aggregate(R0_abs_error ~ model + length + position, grid_est, mean)
write.csv(r0_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "R0_MAE_by_length_and_position.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
w <- reshape(r0_tab[r0_tab$model == V6_LABEL, -1], idvar = "length", timevar = "position", direction = "wide")
names(w) <- sub("R0_abs_error.", "", names(w), fixed = TRUE)
knitr::kable(w[order(w$length), c("length", POSITIONS)], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = paste(V6_LABEL, ": R0 mean absolute error by window length and position"))
cat("Windows tested:", nrow(grid), "\n")
```

```{r grid-compare}
cmp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(grid_est, grid_est$model), function(g)
  data.frame(model = g$model[1], windows = nrow(g), R0_MAE = mean(g$R0_abs_error))))
same61 <- grid_est[grid_est$length == 61 & grid_est$position == "beginning", ]
cmp61  <- aggregate(R0_abs_error ~ model, same61, mean)
names(cmp61)[2] <- "R0_MAE_61_days_beginning"
cmp <- merge(cmp, cmp61, by = "model", all = TRUE)
write.csv(cmp, file.path(OUT_DIR, "R0_MAE_compared.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cmp, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "R0 mean absolute error over all windows each model can read, and on the same 61-day windows from the beginning")
```

```{r grid-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
cols <- c(beginning = "black", middle = "blue", end = "red")
g6 <- r0_tab[r0_tab$model == V6_LABEL, ]
g3 <- r0_tab[r0_tab$model == "v3 (any length, every case)", ]
plot(NA, xlim = range(GRID_LENGTHS), ylim = c(0, max(g6$R0_abs_error, 1)), xlab = "window length (days)",
     ylab = "R0 mean absolute error", main = "Accuracy by window length and position (reported cases)")
for (p in POSITIONS) {
  lines(g6$length[g6$position == p], g6$R0_abs_error[g6$position == p], type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = 2, col = cols[p])
  lines(g3$length[g3$position == p], pmin(g3$R0_abs_error[g3$position == p], 1), type = "b", lty = 3, col = cols[p])
}
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, lty = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 3), col = c(cols, "grey40", "grey40"),
       legend = c(POSITIONS, "v6", "v3 (cut at 1)"))
```

## The other outputs

```{r other-outputs}
th <- test$theta[grid$curve, ]
st_true <- data.frame(lapply(test$states, function(m) m[cbind(grid$curve, grid$start)]))
r2 <- function(e, t) 1 - sum((e - t)^2) / sum((t - mean(t))^2)
out_tab <- data.frame(
  output = c("R0", "log reported share", "log noise (overdispersion)", "weekday swing",
             "log share exposed at window start", "log share infectious at window start", "log share recovered at window start"),
  R2 = c(r2(e6$R0, th$R0), r2(log(e6$report_rate), log(th$report_rate)),
         r2(log(e6$overdispersion), log(th$overdispersion)), r2(e6$weekday_sd, th$weekday_sd),
         vapply(STATES, function(s) r2(log(e6[[s]] + STATE_OFFSET), log(st_true[[s]] + STATE_OFFSET)), 0))
)
write.csv(out_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "all_outputs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(out_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = "R2 over all test windows")
```

# Step 4: a range for R0

As in v4 and v5: for each window, the `r K_NB` calibration windows with the most similar
estimates (and similar `recov`, `incub` and window length) show how far the truth falls
from the estimate. Their errors give the R0 range and the parameter draws for the fit
bands.

```{r calibration}
calib_est <- predict_v6(V6_DIRS, calib$cases, calib$theta)
features <- function(e, known, L) cbind(R0 = e$R0, lr = log(e$report_rate), lo = log(e$overdispersion),
                                        le = log(e$exposed_share + STATE_OFFSET), lrec = log(e$recovered_share + STATE_OFFSET),
                                        recov = known$recov, incub = known$incub, lL = log(L))
F_cal <- features(calib_est, calib$theta, calib$length)
F_mu <- colMeans(F_cal); F_sd <- apply(F_cal, 2, sd)
F_t  <- t(scale(F_cal, F_mu, F_sd))
lg <- function(x) log(x + STATE_OFFSET)
resid <- data.frame(
  R0 = calib$theta$R0 - calib_est$R0,
  lr = log(calib$theta$report_rate) - log(calib_est$report_rate),
  lo = log(calib$theta$overdispersion) - log(calib_est$overdispersion),
  wsd = calib$theta$weekday_sd - calib_est$weekday_sd,
  le = lg(calib$state$exposed_share) - lg(calib_est$exposed_share),
  li = lg(calib$state$infected_share) - lg(calib_est$infected_share),
  lrec = lg(calib$state$recovered_share) - lg(calib_est$recovered_share)
)
neighbours <- function(e, known, L) {
  f <- (features(e, known, L)[1, ] - F_mu) / F_sd
  d <- colSums((F_t - f)^2)
  which(d <= sort(d, partial = K_NB)[K_NB])[seq_len(K_NB)]
}
r0_range <- function(e, nb, probs = c(0.025, 0.975)) e$R0 + quantile(resid$R0[nb], probs, names = FALSE)
draw_parameters <- function(e, known, nb, n) {
  j  <- sample(nb, n, replace = TRUE)
  R0 <- pmax(0.05, e$R0 + resid$R0[j])
  back <- function(est, r) pmax(exp(lg(est) + r) - STATE_OFFSET, 0)
  E  <- back(e$exposed_share, resid$le[j])
  I  <- back(e$infected_share, resid$li[j])
  Rc <- back(e$recovered_share, resid$lrec[j])
  # The three shares are drawn separately; if together they exceed 95% of the
  # population, scale them down so the simulator gets a possible state.
  f  <- pmin(1, 0.95 / pmax(E + I + Rc, 1e-12))
  data.frame(n = known$n, recov = known$recov, incub = known$incub, ptran = e$ptran,
             crate = R0 * known$recov / e$ptran,
             report_rate = pmin(1, exp(log(e$report_rate) + resid$lr[j])),
             overdispersion = exp(log(e$overdispersion) + resid$lo[j]),
             weekday_sd = pmax(0, e$weekday_sd + resid$wsd[j]),
             preval = E * f, start_infected = I * f, start_recovered = Rc * f)
}

set.seed(3)
check <- sample(nrow(grid), min(3000, nrow(grid)))
rng <- t(vapply(check, function(k) r0_range(e6[k, ], neighbours(e6[k, ], known_g[k, ], grid$length[k])), numeric(2)))
inside <- truth_R0[check] >= rng[, 1] & truth_R0[check] <= rng[, 2]
range_tab <- aggregate(cbind(inside = 100 * inside, width = rng[, 2] - rng[, 1]) ~ length, data.frame(length = grid$length[check]), mean)
range_tab <- rbind(range_tab, data.frame(length = "all", inside = 100 * mean(inside), width = mean(rng[, 2] - rng[, 1])))
names(range_tab) <- c("window length", "true R0 inside the 95% range (%)", "mean width")
write.csv(range_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "R0_range_check.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(range_tab, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Step 5: real data

The simulations for a window start from the estimated state at its first day (shares
exposed, infectious and recovered) and include the estimated reporting. v5 is shown on
the 61-day windows it can read (its own R0 range and reporting, as in its report).

```{r real-data}
DD <- params$real_data_dir
covid <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "utah_covid_all_days.csv")); covid$Date <- as.Date(covid$Date)
hhs <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "utah_hhs_hospital_admissions.csv")); hhs$date <- as.Date(substr(hhs$date, 1, 10)) - 1
e1918 <- new.env(); load(file.path(DD, "Flu1918.rda"), envir = e1918)
flu <- hhs$previous_day_admission_influenza_confirmed

real <- list()
add <- function(label, x, y, n, disease) {
  real[[length(real) + 1]] <<- list(label = label, x = x, y = as.numeric(y), n = n,
                                    recov = if (disease == "flu") 0.25 else 1 / 7,
                                    incub = if (disease == "flu") params$flu_incub else params$utah_incub)
}
utah <- tail(covid, 365)
for (L in GRID_LENGTHS) add(sprintf("Utah COVID-19, last %d days", L), tail(utah$Date, L), tail(utah$Daily.Cases, L), 5000, "COVID-19")
for (pos in c("beginning", "middle")) {
  s <- switch(pos, beginning = 1, middle = 153)
  add(sprintf("Utah COVID-19 2024-25, 61 days (%s)", pos), utah$Date[s:(s + 60)], utah$Daily.Cases[s:(s + 60)], 5000, "COVID-19")
}
# The part of a season with the peak: between the last week without cases
# before the peak and the first one after it (like the training windows,
# which never contain a week without cases).
season <- function(from, to, d, y) {
  s <- which(d >= as.Date(from) & d <= as.Date(to)); y <- y[s]
  ma <- as.numeric(stats::filter(y, rep(1 / 7, 7), sides = 2)); pk <- which.max(ma)
  zero_week <- vapply(seq_along(y), function(i) i >= STOP_ZEROS && all(y[(i - STOP_ZEROS + 1):i] == 0), logical(1))
  first <- max(c(0, which(zero_week & seq_along(y) < pk))) + 1
  after <- which(zero_week & seq_along(y) > pk)
  last  <- if (length(after)) after[1] - STOP_ZEROS else length(y)
  list(x = d[s][first:last], y = y[first:last])
}
peak61 <- function(x, y) {
  ma <- as.numeric(stats::filter(y, rep(1 / 7, 7), sides = 2)); end <- min(length(y), which.max(ma) + 7)
  s <- max(1, end - 60); list(x = x[s:(s + 60)], y = y[s:(s + 60)])
}
f1 <- season("2022-09-01", "2023-05-31", hhs$date, flu); f2 <- season("2023-09-01", "2024-04-26", hhs$date, flu)
c3 <- season("2023-06-01", "2023-10-15", covid$Date, covid$Daily.Cases)
b18 <- list(x = seq_along(e1918$Flu1918$incidence), y = e1918$Flu1918$incidence)
add("Utah flu 2022-23, season (no week without admissions)", f1$x, f1$y, 5000, "flu")
add("Utah flu 2023-24, season (no week without admissions)", f2$x, f2$y, 5000, "flu")
add("Baltimore flu 1918, all 92 days", b18$x, b18$y, 10000, "flu")
add("Utah COVID-19 summer 2023, whole wave", c3$x, c3$y, 10000, "COVID-19")
for (d in list(list("Utah flu 2022-23", f1, "flu", 5000), list("Utah flu 2023-24", f2, "flu", 5000),
               list("Baltimore flu 1918", b18, "flu", 10000), list("Utah COVID-19 summer 2023", c3, "COVID-19", 10000))) {
  p <- peak61(d[[2]]$x, d[[2]]$y)
  add(paste0(d[[1]], ", 61 days to a week after the peak"), p$x, p$y, d[[4]], d[[3]])
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(window = vapply(real, `[[`, "", "label"), days = vapply(real, function(r) length(r$y), 0)),
             row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r real-fit}
# v5's own R0 range (its calibration bank), for the 61-day windows.
v5_cal <- read_training_data(file.path(params$v5_calib_dir, "seir_theta.csv"),
                             file.path(params$v5_calib_dir, "seir_observations.csv"), type = "SEIR")
v5_ce <- predict_models(V5_DIRS, v5_cal$observations, v5_cal$theta)
v5_F  <- cbind(R0 = v5_ce$R0, lp = log(v5_ce$preval), lr = log(v5_ce$report_rate), lo = log(v5_ce$overdispersion),
               recov = v5_cal$theta$recov, incub = v5_cal$theta$incub)
v5_mu <- colMeans(v5_F); v5_sd <- apply(v5_F, 2, sd); v5_Ft <- t(scale(v5_F, v5_mu, v5_sd))
v5_res <- data.frame(R0 = v5_cal$theta$R0 - v5_ce$R0, lp = log(v5_cal$theta$preval) - log(v5_ce$preval),
                     lr = log(v5_cal$theta$report_rate) - log(v5_ce$report_rate),
                     lo = log(v5_cal$theta$overdispersion) - log(v5_ce$overdispersion),
                     wsd = v5_cal$theta$weekday_sd - v5_ce$weekday_sd)
v5_draws <- function(e, known, n) {
  f <- (c(e$R0, log(e$preval), log(e$report_rate), log(e$overdispersion), known$recov, known$incub) - v5_mu) / v5_sd
  d <- colSums((v5_Ft - f)^2); nb <- which(d <= sort(d, partial = K_NB)[K_NB])[seq_len(K_NB)]
  j <- sample(nb, n, replace = TRUE); R0 <- pmax(0.05, e$R0 + v5_res$R0[j])
  list(nb = nb, draws = data.frame(n = known$n, recov = known$recov, incub = known$incub,
       preval = pmin(0.9, exp(log(e$preval) + v5_res$lp[j])), ptran = e$ptran, crate = R0 * known$recov / e$ptran,
       report_rate = pmin(1, exp(log(e$report_rate) + v5_res$lr[j])), overdispersion = exp(log(e$overdispersion) + v5_res$lo[j]),
       weekday_sd = pmax(0, e$weekday_sd + v5_res$wsd[j])))
}

band <- function(par_rows, L) {
  sim  <- seir_simulator(ndays = L)
  runs <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(par_rows)), function(i) simulate_from_parameters(sim, as.list(par_rows[i, ]), seed = i), numeric(L))
  data.frame(median = apply(runs, 1, median), lower = apply(runs, 1, quantile, 0.025), upper = apply(runs, 1, quantile, 0.975))
}
score <- function(b, y) c(coverage = 100 * mean(y >= b$lower & y <= b$upper),
                          interval_score = mean((b$upper - b$lower) + 40 * pmax(b$lower - y, 0) + 40 * pmax(y - b$upper, 0)))

set.seed(2026)
fits <- lapply(real, function(w) {
  known <- data.frame(n = w$n, recov = w$recov, incub = w$incub)
  L <- length(w$y)
  e <- predict_v6(V6_DIRS, list(w$y), known)
  # The model reads the informative days only; bands cover the whole window.
  nb <- neighbours(e, known, min(L, informative_days(w$y)))
  out <- list(w = w, e6 = e, r6 = r0_range(e, nb), b6 = band(draw_parameters(e, known, nb, N_REPS), L))
  if (L == 61) {
    e5 <- predict_models(V5_DIRS, matrix(w$y, 1), known)
    d5 <- v5_draws(e5, known, N_REPS)
    out$e5 <- e5; out$r5 <- e5$R0 + quantile(v5_res$R0[d5$nb], c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE)
    out$b5 <- band(d5$draws, L)
  }
  out
})
real_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, function(f) {
  s6 <- score(f$b6, f$w$y); s5 <- if (!is.null(f$b5)) score(f$b5, f$w$y) else c(coverage = NA, interval_score = NA)
  data.frame(window = f$w$label, days = length(f$w$y),
             R0_v6 = f$e6$R0, R0_v6_low = f$r6[1], R0_v6_high = f$r6[2],
             reported_share_v6 = f$e6$report_rate, recovered_at_start_v6 = f$e6$recovered_share,
             coverage_v6 = s6[["coverage"]], interval_score_v6 = s6[["interval_score"]],
             R0_v5 = if (!is.null(f$e5)) f$e5$R0 else NA,
             coverage_v5 = s5[["coverage"]], interval_score_v5 = s5[["interval_score"]])
}))
write.csv(real_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "real_data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(real_tab[, c("window", "days", "R0_v6", "R0_v6_low", "R0_v6_high", "reported_share_v6",
                          "coverage_v6", "interval_score_v6", "R0_v5", "coverage_v5", "interval_score_v5")],
             digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("window", "days", "R0 v6", "low", "high", "reported share v6", "coverage v6 %",
                           "score v6", "R0 v5", "coverage v5 %", "score v5"))
```

Coverage: share of observed days inside the 95% band. Score: interval score (band width
plus 40 times how far each observed day falls outside the band; lower is better).

```{r real-plots, fig.width=13, fig.height=4.2, results="asis"}
for (f in fits) {
  cat("\n\n## ", f$w$label, "\n\n", sep = "")
  panels <- c(list(list(b = f$b6, lab = "v6", r0 = f$e6$R0, r = f$r6, col = "forestgreen")),
              if (!is.null(f$b5)) list(list(b = f$b5, lab = "v5", r0 = f$e5$R0, r = f$r5, col = "purple")))
  ylim <- range(c(f$w$y, unlist(lapply(panels, function(p) c(p$b$lower, p$b$upper)))))
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3.5, 1))
  for (p in panels) {
    s <- score(p$b, f$w$y)
    plot(f$w$x, p$b$median, type = "n", ylim = ylim, xlab = "", ylab = "daily count", cex.main = 0.95,
         main = sprintf("%s: R0 %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)\ncoverage %.0f%% | score %.0f", p$lab, p$r0, p$r[1], p$r[2],
                        s[["coverage"]], s[["interval_score"]]))
    polygon(c(f$w$x, rev(f$w$x)), c(p$b$upper, rev(p$b$lower)), col = adjustcolor(p$col, 0.3), border = NA)
    lines(f$w$x, p$b$median, col = p$col, lwd = 2)
    lines(f$w$x, f$w$y, col = "blue", lwd = 1.5)
  }
  par(op)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# Step 6: other US states

Daily new COVID-19 cases from the Johns Hopkins University COVID-19 repository (county
reports added up per state, January 2020 to March 2023), for six states and three waves.
State counts are far larger than the simulated populations (5,000 to 10,000 people), so
each state's cases are scaled to **cases per 10,000 people** (cases x 10,000 / state
population, rounded) and the models use `n = 10,000`: the model population is a
10,000-person slice of the state. This keeps the shape of a wave and the share of people
infected, which is what R0 depends on; the scaled counts are smoother than real counts
from 10,000 people, so the reported share and noise estimates do not mean much here.

For each wave: the part with the peak (between weeks without cases, if any), read whole
by v6; and the 61 days ending a week after the peak, read by v5 and by v6.

```{r states}
st  <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "state_covid_daily_cases_jhu.csv")); st$date <- as.Date(st$date)
pop <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "state_population.csv"))
STATES_TESTED <- c("Wyoming", "Vermont", "Utah", "Oregon", "New York", "Texas")
WAVES <- list(`fall 2020` = c("2020-09-01", "2021-02-28"), `Delta 2021` = c("2021-06-15", "2021-11-30"),
              `Omicron 2021-22` = c("2021-12-01", "2022-03-31"))
STATE_N <- 10000

fit_v6 <- function(y, known) {
  e  <- predict_v6(V6_DIRS, list(y), known)
  nb <- neighbours(e, known, min(length(y), informative_days(y)))
  list(e = e, r = r0_range(e, nb), b = band(draw_parameters(e, known, nb, N_REPS), length(y)))
}
fit_v5 <- function(y, known) {
  e  <- predict_models(V5_DIRS, matrix(y, 1), known)
  d  <- v5_draws(e, known, N_REPS)
  list(e = e, r = e$R0 + quantile(v5_res$R0[d$nb], c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE), b = band(d$draws, length(y)))
}

set.seed(2027)
state_fits <- list()
for (s in STATES_TESTED) for (wv in names(WAVES)) {
  d <- st[st$state == s, ]
  scaled <- round(d$daily_cases * STATE_N / pop$population[pop$state == s])
  whole  <- season(WAVES[[wv]][1], WAVES[[wv]][2], d$date, scaled)
  in_wave <- d$date >= as.Date(WAVES[[wv]][1]) & d$date <= as.Date(WAVES[[wv]][2])
  w61    <- peak61(d$date[in_wave], scaled[in_wave])
  known  <- data.frame(n = STATE_N, recov = 1 / 7, incub = params$utah_incub)
  state_fits[[paste(s, wv)]] <- list(
    state = s, wave = wv, whole = whole, w61 = w61,
    fits = list(`v5, 61 days` = c(fit_v5(w61$y, known), list(x = w61$x, y = w61$y)),
                `v6, 61 days` = c(fit_v6(w61$y, known), list(x = w61$x, y = w61$y)),
                `v6, whole wave` = c(fit_v6(whole$y, known), list(x = whole$x, y = whole$y))))
}

state_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(state_fits, function(sf) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sf$fits), function(m) {
  f <- sf$fits[[m]]; sc <- score(f$b, f$y)
  data.frame(state = sf$state, wave = sf$wave, fit = m, first_day = format(f$x[1]), days = length(f$y),
             R0 = f$e$R0, R0_low = f$r[1], R0_high = f$r[2],
             coverage = sc[["coverage"]], interval_score = sc[["interval_score"]])
}))))
rownames(state_tab) <- NULL
write.csv(state_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "states.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(state_tab, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("state", "wave", "fit", "first day", "days", "R0", "low", "high", "coverage %", "score"))
```

```{r states-summary}
state_summary <- aggregate(cbind(coverage, interval_score) ~ fit, state_tab, mean)
state_summary$R0_range_width <- aggregate(I(R0_high - R0_low) ~ fit, state_tab, mean)[, 2]
write.csv(state_summary, file.path(OUT_DIR, "states_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(state_summary, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("fit", "mean coverage %", "mean interval score", "mean width of the R0 range"),
             caption = "Mean over the 18 state waves")
```

```{r states-plots, fig.width=13, fig.height=10, results="asis"}
FIT_COLS <- c(`v5, 61 days` = "purple", `v6, 61 days` = "forestgreen", `v6, whole wave` = "darkgreen")
for (s in STATES_TESTED) {
  cat("\n\n## ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  op <- par(mfrow = c(3, 3), mar = c(3, 4, 3.5, 1))
  for (wv in names(WAVES)) {
    sf <- state_fits[[paste(s, wv)]]
    for (m in names(sf$fits)) {
      f <- sf$fits[[m]]; sc <- score(f$b, f$y)
      plot(f$x, f$b$median, type = "n", ylim = range(c(f$y, f$b$lower, f$b$upper)), xlab = "",
           ylab = "cases per 10,000", cex.main = 0.9,
           main = sprintf("%s, %s: R0 %.2f (%.2f-%.2f)\ncoverage %.0f%% | score %.0f", wv, m, f$e$R0, f$r[1], f$r[2],
                          sc[["coverage"]], sc[["interval_score"]]))
      polygon(c(f$x, rev(f$x)), c(f$b$upper, rev(f$b$lower)), col = adjustcolor(FIT_COLS[[m]], 0.3), border = NA)
      lines(f$x, f$b$median, col = FIT_COLS[[m]], lwd = 2)
      lines(f$x, f$y, col = "blue", lwd = 1.2)
    }
  }
  par(op)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```
